name: theme-readme
description: Box theming: copies a README attachment ($README_FILENAME) to every real user's Documents/huitzilopochtli dir as a fixed "README.html" (never the content-addressed attachment name) -- off the Desktop, but readable by snap-confined browsers. $README_FILENAME optional. Auto-created idempotently by boxbuilder/vulndb.py.
script:
#!/bin/sh
# theme-readme -- copies the README attachment ($README_FILENAME) into every real
# user's Documents/huitzilopochtli dir (+ /etc/skel for future users). Forensics
# questions are NOT written here: they are scored, and the agent owns
# Forensics-Questions.txt on the box (it writes the template and re-grades the
# answers each pass).
#
# Why not the Desktop: the desktop stays at exactly the forensics answers file and
# the shortcut launchers (handbook + Scoring Report) -- the handbook .desktop
# points at this copy. Why under $HOME at all: a snap-confined browser (Ubuntu's
# default Firefox) can only see plain $HOME paths -- never /opt, and
# dot-directories are hidden from it too -- so this is the one spot that is off
# the Desktop yet still opens in the team's browser.
set -e

# Resolve a user's XDG Documents dir without sourcing anything as root: extract
# XDG_DOCUMENTS_DIR from user-dirs.dirs by hand and only accept a $HOME-relative or
# absolute value, falling back to $home/Documents.
nakon_mirror_dir() {
    home="$1"
    dirs_file="$home/.config/user-dirs.dirs"
    mirror=""
    if [ -f "$dirs_file" ]; then
        raw=$(grep '^XDG_DOCUMENTS_DIR=' "$dirs_file" | head -n1 | cut -d'"' -f2)
        case "$raw" in
            \$HOME/*) mirror="$home/${raw#\$HOME/}/huitzilopochtli" ;;
            /*) mirror="$raw/huitzilopochtli" ;;
        esac
    fi
    [ -n "$mirror" ] || mirror="$home/Documents/huitzilopochtli"
    echo "$mirror"
}

here="$(pwd)"

# README_FILENAME is content-addressed (see vulndb.py::ensure_attachment --
# "<sha256[:16]>-<basename>", so identical bytes always reuse one attachment).
# That's an internal vulndb storage convention, not something that should ever
# reach a visible filename -- copy it out under a fixed, clean name instead so
# the handbook copy reads as "README.html" and any shortcut that assumes that
# name (e.g. a scenario's own desktop_shortcuts entry) actually resolves.
apply_for() {
    home="$1"
    mirror="$(nakon_mirror_dir "$home")"
    mkdir -p "$mirror"
    if [ -n "$README_FILENAME" ] && [ -f "$here/$README_FILENAME" ]; then
        cp "$here/$README_FILENAME" "$mirror/README.html"
    fi
    # Legacy Desktop copy from the pre-declutter seed: superseded by the
    # Documents copy (the handbook shortcut points there now). Only this one
    # fixed-name file is ever removed.
    rm -f "$home/Desktop/README.html" 2>/dev/null || true
}

awk -F: '($3>=1000 && $3<60000 && $7 !~ /(nologin|false)$/) {print $1":"$6}' /etc/passwd |
while IFS=: read -r nakon_u nakon_h; do
    [ -d "$nakon_h" ] || continue
    apply_for "$nakon_h"
    chown -R "$nakon_u":"$nakon_u" "$(nakon_mirror_dir "$nakon_h")" 2>/dev/null || true
done

# Future users: seed /etc/skel the same way (root:root -- useradd -m fixes it up).
apply_for /etc/skel

exit 0
